pageInfo.subtitle: Master the iconic two-handed technique: tap-pull-hammer triplet loops, multi-string arpeggios, polyphonic tapping, and modern neo-soul touch.
pageInfo.heroDescription: Two-handed fretboard tapping revolutionized electric guitar forever when Eddie Van Halen unleashed 'Eruption' in 1978. By bringing your picking hand onto the fretboard as a second set of fretting fingers, tapping unlocks impossible intervallic leaps, lightning-fast multi-octave arpeggios, and piano-like polyphony far beyond the physical reach of one hand. From classic Van Halen and Randy Rhoads triplet loops to Stanley Jordan's touch guitar and modern neo-soul chord melody tapping (Mateus Asato, Ichika Nito), this masterclass guides you through tap-pull-hammer mechanics, string-to-string navigation, and two-hand muting discipline.

items.text: The Percussive Tap Strike: Strike directly behind the metal fret wire with your index or middle fingertip pad; strike firmly enough to sound cleanly without clattering into the wood.
The Sideways Micro-Pluck: Never lift your tapping finger straight off; flick slightly downward or upward perpendicular to the string to pluck the string for the underlying note.
The Tap-Pull-Hammer Cycle: Internalize the 3-phase engine: Tap with right hand ➔ Pull-off to high fretted note ➔ Pull-off to low fretted note ➔ Hammer back to high note.
Pick Concealment & Finger Selection: Tuck the pick into your palm or curl it into your index knuckle so your middle or index finger is free to tap with accuracy.
The Anchor Thumb: Rest your right thumb lightly on top of the guitar neck for balance and spatial stability rather than hovering unsupported in midair.
Multi-String Arpeggio Tapping: Track your tapping hand across strings in tandem with your fretting hand to outline wide-interval major and minor 7th arpeggios.
Multi-Finger Tapping (Two or More Fingers): Use both the index and middle fingers of the tapping hand to play piano-like polyphonic intervals.
Two-Hand Sympathetic String Muting: Rest the side of your picking-hand palm across lower unplayed strings and use the underside of your fretting index finger to silence higher strings.
Pentatonic & Modal Tapping Extensions: Add a tapped note an octave or fifth above standard pentatonic boxes to extend your blues-rock phrasing range.
Slide-Tapping Transitions: Slide the tapped finger immediately after striking to create crying vocal portamento and futuristic sound effects.

sections.title: The Van Halen Triplet Loop & Single-String Mechanics

exercises.title: The Classic 'Eruption' Triplet Engine
exercises.description: The quintessential tapping workout that started a revolution. On string 2, tap fret 12 with your right-hand middle finger, pull off to fret 8 (pinky), pull off to fret 5 (index), and hammer back to fret 8. In this 4-bar study, shift the tapped note between frets 12, 13, and 15 to outline Am, F, and G chords.

patternNote.text: Eruption Engine: Tap 12 ➔ Pull to 8 ➔ Pull to 5 ➔ Hammer to 8 (repeated seamlessly)

notation.title: The Classic Van Halen Tapping Loop Across Chord Shifts
notation.staveTitle: 16th-Note Two-Handed Tapping Motor Across Shifting Tapped Frets

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Ensure each of the 4 notes has identical volume and duration. Do not rush the pull-offs; let the metronome click guide every downbeat.

exercises.title: Major & Minor Tapped Triad Cycles
exercises.description: Transfer the tapping engine to the high E string to outline complete arpeggios: A minor (Tap 12, pull 8, pull 5), C major (Tap 15, pull 12, pull 8), and D major (Tap 17, pull 14, pull 10). Notice how the shifting positions outline soaring harmony.

notation.title: Tapped Arpeggio Triad Cycles on String 1
notation.staveTitle: Traversing Shifting Tapped Triads Along the High E String

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Keep your tapping finger perpendicular to the fretboard. When shifting positions between bars, lead with your eyes to ensure the tap lands squarely behind the fret wire.

exercises.title: 4-Note Tapped Quad Loop (16th-Note Grid)
exercises.description: Instead of keeping the tapped note stationary, move the tapped finger across frets 12, 13, 15, and 13 within the same measure while the fretting hand holds fret 5 and 8 stationary. This develops independent right-hand fretboard mobility.

patternNote.text: Moving Tap: Tapped note moves [12 ➔ 13 ➔ 15 ➔ 13] while left hand anchors [8-5]

notation.title: Moving Tapped Finger 16th-Note Grid
notation.staveTitle: Independent Tapping Hand Navigation Across Consecutive Strings

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Notice how moving the tapped finger creates a melodic singing top line above the static fretted ostinato. Maintain a relaxed right-hand wrist.

sections.title: Multi-String Arpeggios, Position Shifts & Master Etude

exercises.title: Multi-String Pentatonic Tapping Run
exercises.description: Bring two-handed tapping into your blues-rock soloing. Fret the classic A minor pentatonic box at fret 5 while tapping fret 12 across strings 1 through 6. This adds an extended octave layer to standard pentatonic licks with zero picking effort.

patternNote.text: Pentatonic Extension: Tap fret 12 across all 6 strings above Position 1 pentatonic

notation.title: Multi-String Pentatonic Tapping Cascades
notation.staveTitle: Traversing All Six Strings in A Minor Pentatonic with Tapped Octaves

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Keep your picking-hand palm resting lightly across lower unplayed strings to eliminate open-string roar as your tapping finger travels across strings.

exercises.title: Two-Handed Arpeggio Crossing (Randy Rhoads Style)
exercises.description: Randy Rhoads revolutionized heavy metal soloing on Ozzy Osbourne's 'Crazy Train' with two-handed arpeggio cascades. In this exercise, both hands descend across strings 1, 2, 3, and 4 in synchronized motion over Am, G, F, and E chords.

patternNote.text: Two-Hand Tracking: Right hand taps high notes ➔ Left hand pulls off across 4 strings

notation.title: Randy Rhoads Multi-String Tapped Arpeggios
notation.staveTitle: Multi-String Descending Tapped Arpeggio Cascades Across Am - G - F - E

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Notice the diagonal line: both hands jump together to the new string on every beat. Synchronize the right-hand tap with the left-hand position shift.

exercises.title: Two-Finger Polyphonic Chord Tapping
exercises.description: Touch-guitar pioneer Stanley Jordan and modern neo-soul virtuoso Mateus Asato use multiple fingers on the tapping hand to play piano-like polyphonic chords. Tap two strings simultaneously using your right index and middle fingers while the left hand holds bass roots.

patternNote.text: Polyphonic Touch: Left hand frets bass root ➔ Right hand taps 2-string harmony simultaneously

notation.title: Polyphonic Two-Finger Chord Tapping Study
notation.staveTitle: Interleaving Fretted Bass Notes with Simultaneous Two-Finger Tapped Double Stops

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Tap both strings with equal velocity so both harmony notes ring at identical volume. This technique transforms a single guitar into a full acoustic piano.

exercises.title: The Master Tapping Etude: From Triplet Shred to Neo-Soul Touch
exercises.description: This culminating 4-measure etude synthesizes the entire spectrum of two-handed tapping: high-velocity Van Halen triplet runs over Am, multi-string arpeggios over F, modern slide-tapped double stops over C, and singing high-octave resolutions over G.

patternNote.text: Complete Tapping Synthesis: Triplet Loops + Multi-String Arpeggios + Polyphonic Double Stops

notation.title: Master Two-Handed Tapping Virtuoso Etude
notation.staveTitle: Comprehensive 4-Bar Virtuoso Tapping Etude Across Am - F - C - G

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Use a light overdrive or clean boost. Focus on dynamics: make the opening run crack with aggression, then let the chord taps ring like a warm electric piano.

tips.title: Tapping Mastery Insights, Pitfalls & Daily Workout

items.title: 3 Mistakes That Kill Two-Handed Tapping
items: Lifting Straight Off on Tapped Pull-Offs: Simply lifting the tapping finger off the string results in a quiet, dying note. You must execute a crisp sideways micro-pluck to re-energize the string.
Open String Sympathetic Roar: Because both hands are on the fretboard, open strings love to buzz and squeal. You must rest the edge of your right palm across the lower strings at all times.
Mushy Tapping Finger Contact: Hesitant tapping produces double-clicks and buzz. Strike decisively right behind the fret wire with a firm, spring-loaded finger motion.

items.title: Masters of Two-Handed Tapping
items: Eddie Van Halen: The revolutionary pioneer who introduced two-handed tapping to the world on 'Eruption', defining hard rock lead guitar for generations.
Stanley Jordan: Jazz virtuoso who revolutionized touch technique by playing independent counterpoint and four-part piano chords with all 8 fingers.
Randy Rhoads: Heavy metal icon who combined classical minor arpeggios with lightning-fast multi-string tapping on Ozzy Osbourne masterpieces.
Mateus Asato: Modern guitar phenom known for soulful, vocal, neo-soul tapping chords that blend seamlessly into vocal melodic phrasing.

items.title: The 15-Minute Daily Tapping Workout
items: Block 1: Van Halen Triplet Calibration (5 min) - Practice the classic 12-8-5 triplet cycle at 80 BPM, focusing entirely on equal note volume and crisp sideways pull-offs.
Block 2: Multi-String Pentatonic Traversal (5 min) - Cycle tapped pentatonics across all six strings, building right-hand palm muting discipline on lower strings.
Block 3: Two-Handed Arpeggio Crossing (5 min) - Practice the Randy Rhoads descending arpeggio pattern across strings 1 through 4, locking in position shifts.
